What the numbers say

For the session of Tuesday, November 3, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (26 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as mixed. SPY is below its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is down and realised volatility is in the calm band.

8 of 26 tickers (31%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 17 of 25 (68%) above their 200-day average. That sits between the model's 30% and 55% breadth thresholds, so breadth alone decides nothing here. On the day 13 rose and 13 fell; the median move was +0.04%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Technology had the strongest average move at +1.50% and Consumer Discretionary the weakest at −0.47%, a spread of 1.97 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 1.71 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

3 tickers have a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (GOOG, INTC, MRVL), and none is at or above 70. An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-02), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 38% to 31%, and the regime reading stayed mixed.
